note: The canonical feature list. Machine-readable so every client can read it and so a gate can check it, rather than a table that drifts. Validated by website/src/feature-parity.test.ts. See contracts/feature-parity/SKILL.md.

statuses.shipped: Implemented and working on this platform.
statuses.partial: Partly implemented. `gap` says what is missing.
statuses.planned: Specified here, not built on this platform yet.

features.title: The solar system to scale, positioned from real ephemerides
features.why: The product. Everything else hangs off it.

features.title: All 32 bodies: Sun, 8 planets, 23 moons
features.why: A solar system missing Titan and the Galileans is not a true representation.

features.title: Select and focus any body
features.why: Navigation. Without it the system view is a poster.

features.title: Body data panel with provenance on every figure
features.why: contracts/numbers-come-from-the-engine. A number without its source is a guess.

features.title: What the clock rate means for the body in view
features.why: "1 day/s" is accurate and tells a viewer nothing. Someone read Earth spinning once a second as a bug.

features.title: Play, pause, reverse, jump to now, and rate presets from real time upward
features.why: Seeing a year pass is the point of a simulator.

features.title: Orbit paths sampled from the solver that positions the body
features.why: An idealised ellipse is decoration. Sampling the real solver draws the path the body will actually follow.

features.title: Real NASA and USGS surface imagery
features.why: A flat tint is a placeholder. The imagery is data too.

features.title: City lights on the dark side, masked by the lighting geometry
features.why: The clearest evidence a simulator can give that the dark side is night rather than empty space.

features.title: Saturn's rings at their real extent, tilted with the planet
features.why: Saturn without rings is not Saturn.

features.title: Day, terminator and night viewing angles
features.why: The thing worth seeing on a planet is usually the line between its day and its night.

features.title: Frame a planet together with its moons
features.why: Framing on the planet alone crops the Moon 1,300 pixels off screen, which reads as a missing Moon.

features.title: Continuous zoom from system scale to a surface, with a floating origin
features.why: Ten orders of magnitude. contracts/floating-origin.

ios.gap: The floating origin is real: the focused body's position is subtracted in Double and renderPosition is the one Float conversion. What differs from the web is continuity. The scene's scale is chosen per focused body rather than per frame, so moving between system scale and surface scale is a step at the focus change rather than a continuous fly-through. The web keeps everything in metres with a logarithmic depth buffer, which SceneKit does not expose. Both reach a surface; only one does it without a seam.

features.title: Craters from real elevation data, streamed as tiles
features.why: Real LRO LOLA topography, with the resolution limit stated rather than letting someone conclude the Moon is flat.

features.title: Full N-body mode where every body pulls every other
features.why: The only mode in which a mass you add changes anything. contracts/gravity-modes.

features.title: Launch an asteroid and propagate it under real gravity
features.why: Where it ends up, with the impact energy, gated against Chelyabinsk, Tunguska and Chicxulub.

features.title: Rocket ascent and payload to orbit
features.why: Inverted gate against ULA's published figures; see the playbook's P7.

features.title: Physics demonstrations, each reproducing a published value
features.why: Kepler's third law, light travel time, solar irradiance, Mercury's relativistic precession.

features.title: Ask about the solar system, answered through engine-backed tools
features.why: contracts/numbers-come-from-the-engine. The model narrates; the engine owns every figure.

features.title: Star background
features.why: Depth cue, and it should be the real sky.

features.title: Orientation from the full IAU rotational elements
features.why: contracts/rotation-and-poles. A sidereal rate alone gives the right speed and the wrong prime meridian.

features.title: Hide every panel to see the scene unobstructed
features.why: The panels are the point right up until you want to look at the planet, at which moment they are covering it.

features.title: An obvious way back out to the whole solar system
features.why: Focusing the Sun has always been the system view and nothing said so; someone had to ask how to unfocus a planet.

features.title: Habitability assessment: what it would take to live on this body
features.why: The question people actually ask about a planet, answered from the same contracts that position it. Every figure comes from engine/src/habitability.ts, so the two clients cannot quote different masses, temperatures or mirror areas for the same body.

features.title: Ride a launched object: fly with it and watch from on board
features.why: Launching used to leave the camera wherever it was, so the departure happened off screen. Both clients now focus the body the object leaves from and can put the floating origin on the object itself, which turns the existing camera into an onboard one. The interpolation that places it between integrator samples is engine/src/propagate.ts trajectoryStateAt, gated by the trajectory-interpolation conformance domain so the two riders agree.

features.title: Markers for bodies too small to resolve
features.why: From anywhere useful in the solar system most bodies are well under a pixel across, and drawing them larger would be a lie about scale. A soft dot in the body's own colour fades in exactly as the real sphere stops being resolvable, so scale stays honest and nothing becomes invisible. The web has done this from the start; iOS had nothing, so Phobos rendered at 0.46 pixels and a viewer reported that moons were missing. The feature was never listed here, which is why the parity gate had nothing to compare.

features.title: Body labels, including pointers to bodies that are off screen
features.why: A marker says something is here; only a label says what. The case it exists for is the off-screen one: focused on Earth at six radii the Moon is sixty radii away and not in frame at all, so there is nothing on screen to look harder at. A label clamped to the edge nearest it, with a bearing, turns 'it is missing' into 'it is that way'. Placement is engine/src/labels.ts, gated by the labels conformance domain so both clients clamp and thin identically.

features.title: Stand on the surface: real photographs taken on other worlds
features.why: Asked for as a way to look around a world with real pictures rather than anything generated. That constraint is the design: NASA's library is full of artist's impressions and computed perspective views rendered from radar, and a search for 'Venus surface' returns a Magellan elevation model drawn as a landscape that looks exactly like a photograph and is not one. Every image is a curated asset id, and ./build.sh imagery re-resolves each one and rejects anything whose own description calls it a concept, an illustration or a perspective view. The gaps are the other half: five worlds have ever been photographed from their own surface, and each body with none says why.
